title: What is useRef and when is it the right tool?
description: DOM refs, mutable boxes that survive renders, the latest-ref pattern, and why ref mutations don't re-render.

data.text: **Question:** What is useRef and when is it the right tool?

`useRef` returns a mutable container whose `.current` value **persists across renders without causing them**. It has two main jobs: (1) holding a reference to a DOM node (or any imperative instance — video player, canvas, WebSocket, IntersectionObserver) so you can interact with it directly; and (2) storing mutable values that must survive re-renders — timestamps of the last render, previous props, timers, abort controllers — without triggering re-renders when they change. If a value should visibly change in the UI, it belongs in state; if changing it must NOT re-render, it belongs in a ref.

**How it works:**
- `const ref = useRef(initial)` returns the **same object** every render; only `.current` changes. That object identity is why effects can depend on it safely
- Passing `ref={inputRef}` to a JSX element populates `.current` with the DOM node after mount (and nulls it on unmount)
- Writing `ref.current = x` is a plain mutation — React doesn't know, doesn't re-render, no scheduling involved
- Initial value is used only on first render; `useRef()` with no argument gives `undefined`

**When it's the right tool:**
- **Imperative DOM interaction**: focus(), scrollIntoView(), measuring with getBoundingClientRect, playing media
- **Non-DOM instances**: `new WebSocket(...)`, `new IntersectionObserver(...)`, chart-library instances — things created once and managed by hand
- **Mutable values that shouldn't trigger renders**: last-click timestamp, previous props for comparison, an `AbortController` to cancel stale work, a timer handle
- **The latest-ref pattern**: effects that should read the newest props/state without re-subscribing — store them in a ref updated each render, so a long-lived subscription (keydown listener, interval) calls `ref.current()` without re-registering
- Scheduling without effects: `useRef` + `requestAnimationFrame` handles where state would loop

**When it's the wrong tool:**
- Rendering data derived from it — refs don't trigger renders; the UI will show stale values
- Reading `.current` during render to make decisions — it may be from a previous render; use state or the render-phase read pattern (`const prev = useRef(); const delta = value - prev.current`) only with care
- As a substitute for state management — no subscriptions, no reactivity
- Passing ref-created values to memoized children — mutations won't update them

**Related mechanics:**
- `forwardRef` (or ref as a prop in React 19) lets a parent reach a child's DOM node
- Callback refs (`ref={(node) => ...}`) run on mount/unmount — useful for measuring or wiring instances, with cleanup
- Refs in StrictMode mount/unmount/remount in dev — a ref set to an instance must tolerate double-invocation of effects

data.title: DOM ref, mutable box, and the latest-ref pattern

data.text:
Interviewers want to assess:
- The core rule: state for visible data, refs for imperative handles and invisible mutable values
- Knowing ref identity is stable across renders and mutations don't re-render
- Practical patterns: latest-ref, abort controllers, callback refs for measuring
- Awareness that reading refs during render can be stale

items: Storing rendered data in a ref — the UI never updates because no re-render is triggered
Reading ref.current during render for branching logic — it can hold a previous render's value
Re-creating a listener effect because the ref holds a function that changes — use the latest-ref pattern
Mutating ref.current and expecting memoized children or effects to react
Using a ref where state + effect already solves it (manual subscription to your own state)
Forgetting that StrictMode remounts effects in dev — instance refs need double-effect safety
Why does the latest-ref pattern let an effect run once while still seeing fresh props?
How do callback refs differ from object refs, and when do you need the cleanup form?
What changed about refs in React 19 (ref as a prop, cleanup functions)?
How would you implement a stopwatch with refs and one state for display?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useRef: stable mutable box; .current changes without re-renders
Use for DOM nodes, imperative instances, timers, controllers, latest values
Never for data the UI should display — that's state
Latest-ref pattern keeps long-lived listeners fresh without re-subscribing
data.takeaway: Refs are React's escape hatch to the imperative world: hold handles and invisible mutable state there, and keep anything the user sees in state.
